locations.name: South Holston River
locations.description: The South Holston River has quietly gained the reputation of one of the best tailwater fisheries in the entire eastern United States. The river is known for its Sulphur hatches that begin in late June and last until early fall.

locations.name: Watauga River
locations.description: This tailwater river begins below the Wilbur Dam and flows through the small Appalachian town of Elizabethton, Tennessee. Wild Brown Trout flourish here and the river has not been stocked with fish since the early 2000's. Access can be found easily at many road pull offs or at the Sycamore Shoals State Park.

locations.name: Hiwassee River
locations.description: One of the most scenic rivers in the state, the Hiwasssee River runs through the Cherokee National Forest in Southeast Tennessee. With an incredibly wide river bed, it feels very much like some of the larger rivers out West. The river is also a big attraction for kayakers and white water rafting trips.

locations.name: Caney Fork River
locations.description: Located about one hour east of Nashville, this is the most popular destination for fly fishing in Middle Tennessee. Construction on the Center Hill Dam has caused a negative effect on trout populations in recent years, however efforts from the Nashville Trout Unlimited chapter have led to improvements to the fishery.

locations.name: Elk River
locations.description: The Elk is one of the lesser known Tennessee tailwaters, and is located just down the road from the Jack Daniels Distillery in Lynchburg. The river provides a quiet pastoral setting for those who wish to escape the crowds.

locations.name: Tellico Lake
locations.description: Located just south of Maryville, TN, Tellico Lake is one of the most productive lakes year round. It is home of the Tellico Nymph, a fly pattern used by fly fisherman the world over.

locations.name: Chilhowee Lake
locations.description: Chilhowee Lake is an impoundment on the Little Tennessee River that was built in the 1950s and is part of a chain of lakes that begin in North Carolina and end at the confluence of the Tennessee River. In addition to trout, this is a great lake to fish for smallmouth or largemouth bass.

locations.name: Wilbur Lake
locations.description: This tiny mountain lake is situated just above the Watauga River and provides excellent access with nearly half the lake accessable from the road. Multiple picnic shelters and a small boat ramp make it a great option for families with young children.

locations.name: Abrams Creek
locations.description: Abrams Creek is considered by many to be one of the best wild trout streams in the Southeast. Located in the Great Smoky Mountains State Park it drains into the Cades Cove Recreation area. Access is remote and may require a long hike in and out so plan accordingly.

locations.name: Doe River
locations.description: The Doe River an excellent freestone stream with a lot to offer. A tributary of the Watauga River, it begins in Roan Mountain State Park and flows through the scenic Doe River Gorge. Water can rise quickly here so be sure to keep an eye on the weather. Many sections of this river are still recovering from the extensive flooding caused by Hurricane Helene.

reports.title: Late Summer Trout Bite
reports.body: Caught a very nice 22 inch rainbow trout on an olive Wooly Bugger just below the dam around sunset.

reports.title: Early Afternoon Caddis Hatch Success
reports.body: Caddis flies are still hatching on the Watauga. Caught 4 rainbow trout this afternoon on size 16-18 caddis dry flies.

reports.title: Wild Brook Trout found in Deep Plunge Pools
reports.body: Had a great day fishing on this beautiful wild mountain stream. Caught 3 native brook trout using nymphs in deep pools below waterfalls.

reports.title: Brook Trout on Streamers
reports.body: Caught 5 Brook Trout on small white size #12 streamer flies below the dam.

reports.title: Rainbow Trout in shallows
reports.body: Caught nine rainbow trout near the shoreline with dry flies.

reports.title: Brown Trout moving to spawning areas
reports.body: The Brown Trout have begun their spawning pattern. Be careful to avoid stepping on their eggs.

reports.title: High Water Level & Fast Current!
reports.body: With the recent heavy rains the river level is much higher than usual and flows aren't suitable for fishing. Other nearby locations such as the South Holston River or the Watauga River might be better options.

reports.title: Lots of rainbow trout recently stocked here!
reports.body: The local fisheries have recently stocked this lake with lots of small rainbow trout between 10-12" long. These can be easily caught on brightly colored Egg or Worm patterns. Great place for a beginner!

reports.title: Large Lake Trout Caught Very Deep
reports.body: This lake is filled with gigantic lake trout! They can be caught using heavily weighted sinking lines and large streamer patterns fished near the bottom!

reports.title: Early Morning Catch
reports.body: Caught several fish on small Blue Wing Olive dry flies early in the morning today.

reports.title: Freezing Cold Temps = Very Few Fish
reports.body: It's getting very cold on these streams up in the higher elevations. Only caught two very small trout all day here.
